# 23 — Splendor

**Built and playing** — `game/games/splendor.json`, generated by
`tools/make_splendor.py`, tested by `tests/integration/splendor.lua`.

Two seats: the supply is the 2-player one. Everything else is in — reserve both
ways, the gold wildcard, the three-card cap, the noble visit with a choice among
ties, the ten-token limit, the last round played out, the fewest-cards tiebreak.

## The one that mattered

**The research checked five mechanics and skipped the purchase**, which is the
only one that was ever in doubt. The discount is the whole of what makes
Splendor an engine builder, and worked through it is three clamped subtractions
per colour:

```
due_c    = max(0, printed_c - bonus_c)      what the discounts leave to pay
short_c  = max(0, due_c - tokens_c)         what gold has to cover, per colour
gold_due = Σ short_c
```

The amount grammar has products only — no subtraction, no `min`, no `max`. On
paper that is a real gap.

**It is not, because `stat_damage` against a floor of zero *is* `max(0, a - b)`.**
Every line above is one action and nothing is left over. Affordability comes out
the same way: `max(0, 1 + gold - gold_due)` is 1 exactly when the gold covers
the bill, so the gate is an ordinary `needs` reading one number and an
unaffordable card dims like any other.

Two things had to already be true. **A stat's floor is declared, and a floor is
what makes subtraction stop** — these are `hidden` stats with `min: 0`, which
also keeps eighteen scratch numbers per card out of the HUD. And **the
arithmetic runs on the card**, through `activate_zone` over the market rows, so
it is written once on a tag and ninety cards share it.

So the "zero new primitives" verdict stands and its reasoning does not. Splendor
does ask for clamped subtraction; the engine has had it since stats had floors.

## Two smaller things

- **`seat: "next"` is ignored on an `automatic` phase.** `flow.settle` rotates
  only in the branch handling a phase a player acts in, so bookkeeping that
  opens a turn goes in the *input* phase's own `actions` and routes back to a
  seatless copy. lor arrived at the same pair independently. Making `seat` work
  on automatic phases is probably right and nothing has wanted it.
- **An ability is gated by its cost and its phase, and nothing else** — no
  `needs`. So every conditional ability here is a cost that reads correctly as
  one: `reserve_slots` is spent by reserving, `first_take` is what taking two of
  a colour spends, `plenty` is what "four still in the stack" spends. Where the
  gate is not a spend, the button is a card played out of a `hand` instead,
  because `play` does take a `needs`.

**The art is procedural, deliberately.** Splendor's art is Asmodee's, so none
was downloaded, and it loses nothing: a development card has no printed name,
and what a player reads off it is the cost (the title), the bonus colour (the
plate, through a style), the prestige (a badge) and the tier (the generated
shape). The fan transcriptions the data came from are unlicensed too, which is
why only the numbers were taken, from three sources cross-checked
programmatically.
